name: Diane Abbott
role: British MP for Hackney North and Stoke Newington (since 1987), former shadow home secretary
summary: Abbott supports public services, public ownership, progressive taxation and migrants’ rights, alongside opposition to nuclear weapons and party leadership policies she considers excessively market-oriented. Her civil-liberties positions coexist with support for additional police officers; she supports abortion rights and transgender inclusion, while expressing serious reservations about assisted-dying legislation.

notes:
Covered council and parliamentary career, 2010 leadership proposals, shadow ministerial speeches, civil liberties, policing, migration, reproductive and transgender rights, and 2024–2026 evidence. Downloaded the complete Fabian pamphlet and isolated her pages from other candidates, plus full immigration and conference speeches, the PoliticsHome interview and the July 2024 Morning Star issue; read her printed page 21 directly. Later columns confirm her public-ownership and public-investment positions. Her 2026 assisted-dying vote is read alongside her explicit conditional acceptance in principle, hence low confidence rather than categorical opposition. The 2022 NATO statement withdrawal supersedes its pre-invasion wording. Her identification with socialism does not establish worker ownership or abolition of the state. Opposition to ID cards based partly on their alleged ineffectiveness does not answer whether all surveillance is acceptable if it prevents terrorism. Support for bank regulation does not establish a prohibition on anonymous payments. Her 2023 and 2025 statements distinguishing colour-based racism from anti-Jewish, Irish and Traveller prejudice were reviewed as a major controversy; no specific segregation, intermarriage, boycott or denial-of-rights position follows from that definitional claim. Early remarks about Mao do not establish support for a particular governing institution. Reviewed culture, world, ecology, technology and globalism items and every remaining null against the evidence. No inference from party membership, relatives or endorsements. No inferred answers.
